accepted_selected_source_facts: 228/509 are actual Rust line!() arguments in retained x86_cpu_helpers.rs save/copy allocation calls. CPU_FILE deliberately emits arch/x86_64/kernel/cpu.c; they are not physical line numbers in cpu.c text.

Rust release_fp_regs returns early on null fp_regs; the pages-only release marker is emitted only in its non-null branch, before _ihk_mc_free_pages and before the pointer slot is cleared. Marker contains no pointer/TID.

Allocator ADD logs the allocation result pointer; REMOVE logs addr_entry.addr. Entry keys are shared file/line allocation groups, not unique tracking-entry addresses. Final DELETE follows removal when alloc_count reaches zero.

kprintf locks individual writes; allocator entry/add and remove/delete span lock releases. One CPU does not imply whole allocator-operation atomicity. Current neighbor/final-delete filters are useful conservative candidate constraints, not a new thread or atomicity proof.

Unchanged pinned native_diagnostic._validate_manifest/evaluate remain called and require exact AVX payload/oracle, stream completion, procfs-empty, trace/retirement/release, QMP shutdown and teardown. Evaluator keeps native_acceptance=false.

findings.predicate: Current consumer accepts raw length CAP-1=4190207. Ring writer uses exactly len-1 retained occupancy after overwriting the head. A newline-terminated overwritten prefix can therefore pass size/newline and contain a complete apparently fresh allocation/release sequence while hiding prior pointer history. The seen-pointer reuse test covers only retained text.

A stricter <CAP-1 threshold is a candidate minimum only after binding actual reader fixed length/nonshifting behavior and accounting for its wrapped-bottom strnlen behavior. Do not label an unknown-history ring complete.
